model_reported.summary: Selected a one-variable tile-size increase from 256 to 512 while retaining the 128-thread CTA and one target per thread.

model_reported.name: inspecter-environnement
model_reported.summary: This proposal uses standard CUDA shared memory and barriers, not an architecture-specific instruction; the controller build will validate the 8 KiB launch allocation on the frozen target.

model_reported.name: consulter-documentation-technique
model_reported.summary: No version-sensitive API or uncertain synchronization behavior is introduced; conventional CUDA shared-memory staging and block barriers are used.

model_reported.name: evaluer-performances
model_reported.summary: Used supplied valid timing observations only as context for the tile-size experiment; no new performance outcome or speedup is claimed.

proposal.hypothesis: Keeping one target per thread and a 128-thread CTA while doubling the source tile from 256 to 512 should halve the tile-loop and barrier-pair count for each target block. The tradeoff is twice the shared-memory footprint (8 KiB) and four cooperative loads per thread per tile, so official timing must determine whether the reduced synchronization overhead helps.

retained: Changed the launch to 128 threads/targets per CTA with 8192 bytes of dynamic shared memory for 512 compact source records.
Cooperatively staged bounded source chunks and synchronized before use and before replacing each chunk, with inactive tail threads participating in barriers.
Kept one target and force accumulator per active thread, skipped self-interactions by global index, preserved the force and integration expressions, and guarded partial tiles and target tails.

proposal.hypothesis: With the existing 128-thread CTA, increasing the source tile from 512 to 1024 lets each CTA process twice as many sources per tile iteration, potentially reducing synchronization and loop overhead. retained: Increase the cooperative source tile to 1024 entries and set dynamic shared memory to 16384 bytes, consistent with four 32-bit fields per entry.

Keep the 128-thread launch configuration, one target and accumulator per active thread, bounded partial-tile consumption, global-index self-exclusion, unconditional synchronization, and guarded output coverage.
